summary:
Planetary Analog Explorer is an interactive research tool that helps people find places on Earth that resemble the Moon and Mars. Using NASA satellite imagery, planetary data, and interactive maps, it explores locations such as Ladakh, the Atacama Desert, and Hawaii.

Users can compare geological features, terrain, temperatures, and surface conditions across Earth and other planetary bodies. The app also includes interactive visualizations and a clear suitability score, which shows how closely a location matches a particular environment.

Built with Python, JavaScript, Leaflet, and NASA open-data services such as GIBS and PDS, Planetary Analog Explorer is designed to support space research, student projects, and future mission planning.
details:
TRINITY – Planetary Analog Explorer

Earth • Moon • Mars | Exploring Earth to prepare for life beyond it

Project Description

TRINITY is an interactive planetary research and exploration web application designed to identify and analyze locations on Earth that resemble geological and environmental conditions found on the Moon and Mars.

The project uses satellite imagery, geospatial information and scientific datasets to discover terrestrial analog environments that can help researchers understand extraterrestrial landscapes and prepare for future robotic and human space missions.

TRINITY focuses on three major research areas: Earth, Moon and Mars. Users can explore terrestrial analog locations such as Ladakh, the Atacama Desert and Hawaiian volcanic landscapes, examine their geological characteristics, and compare them with selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

The application aims to make planetary research more accessible through interactive maps, visual comparisons, environmental analysis and analog suitability scoring.

Key Features

  1. Earth Analog Explorer: Discover and explore Earth locations that resemble lunar and Martian environments.
  2. Moon Explorer: Investigate lunar craters, volcanic regions, surface conditions and potential base locations.
  3. Mars Explorer: Explore Martian terrain, ancient river deltas, geological formations and potential landing sites.
  4. Planetary Comparison: Compare terrain, temperature, surface materials, water availability and other environmental characteristics.
  5. Analog Suitability Score: Calculate an explainable score indicating how suitable an Earth location is for a particular planetary research objective.
  6. Interactive Dashboard: Visualize satellite imagery, location information, scientific parameters and comparison charts.
  7. Research Reports: Generate reports containing selected locations, comparisons, observations and data sources.

3. How NASA data is used

NASA open datasets are an important part of TRINITY because they provide real scientific observations rather than relying entirely on manually entered information.

Primary NASA data source: Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS)

TRINITY uses NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) to display satellite imagery of Earth. GIBS provides standardized WMS and WMTS services that can be integrated into interactive maps.

Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS)+1

The application can use this imagery to:

  • Examine geological formations and surface patterns.
  • Explore selected terrestrial analog locations.
  • Observe environmental and land-surface changes over time.
  • Visually compare Earth environments with lunar and Martian landscapes.

Additional NASA source: Planetary Data System (PDS)

NASA's Planetary Data System provides archived observations from planetary missions. TRINITY can use selected lunar and Mars datasets for surface imagery, topography and geological comparisons.

Planetary Data System+1

Official resources:

  • NASA GIBS API
  • NASA Planetary Data System

4. Future implications and applications

TRINITY has the potential to evolve into a more advanced planetary research and mission-planning platform.

1. AI-powered analog discovery: Use machine learning to identify Earth locations with geological and environmental characteristics similar to the Moon and Mars.

2. Permanent lunar base planning: Analyze terrain slope, illumination, temperature and potential water-ice indicators to help evaluate candidate lunar settlement regions.

3. Mars landing-site assessment: Compare surface geology, elevation, terrain roughness and mineralogical characteristics to help identify promising landing and exploration areas.

4. 3D planetary visualization: Introduce interactive 3D terrain models of Earth, Moon and Mars using elevation datasets.

5. Advanced NASA data integration: Incorporate Landsat, ASTER, MODIS, NISAR, LRO and Mars mission datasets for more detailed scientific analysis.

6. Robotic exploration preparation: Help researchers investigate rover mobility, drilling conditions, surface hazards and subsurface exploration.

7. Research report generation: Generate scientific reports with maps, satellite imagery, comparisons, suitability scores and data references.

5. Project vision

The long-term vision of TRINITY is to create a unified platform that connects Earth-based research with planetary exploration.

By combining NASA satellite observations, planetary mission datasets, geospatial technologies and AI-based analysis, TRINITY aims to help researchers discover useful terrestrial analogs and support the planning of future robotic missions and permanent human settlements beyond Earth.

TRINITY – Three Worlds. One Exploration Platform.
